title: ZTF DR24 fits do not give a stable decay mechanism for the 2020 ZTF J0436+5728 event
abstract: We test whether the known 5.910-hour modulation of ZTF J0436+5728 fades through common amplitude decay or Gaussian orbital spreading. We fit ZTF DR24 detections over 245 days from the published 2020 event start. The main r-band fit uses 205 measurements and three harmonics. Common decay has a weighted residual score 4.64 below spreading. A conditional test with random residual signs for each night gives a tail estimate of 0.0175 under the fitted spreading model. This preference is not stable. Two harmonics favor spreading by 8.76, and joint g/r fits favor it by 9.27. A local correction from 18 nearby stars reduces the main difference to 0.20. Removing the dense night and changing night weights retain the main r-band preference. The target varies much more than local controls, but these checks do not locate the signal in images. The data do not identify a decay mechanism. The models assume a fixed flux profile and simple damping laws. Detection loss, optical saturation, sparse later sampling, source-specific errors and changes in dust production remain open. No new event, planet, dust-loss rate or independent active-state confirmation is claimed. Original code, aggregate results, figures, exact input paths and hashes, and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included. Raw external data stay outside the publication.

display.caption: The preferred decay model changes with harmonic order and passband. A local comparison-star correction nearly removes the main score difference. Harmonic-amplitude errors are formal errors under a fixed-frequency fit.
Night-level residual-sign tests are conditional on the main three-harmonic r-band fit. The target varies more than 18 local comparison stars on the densely sampled half orbit.
